headline: Humanoid robots are being trained to restock shelves at a Føtex supermarket near Copenhagen, with human operators guiding them for now and independent night work targeted for early 2027.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: reported on 11 Oct 2026 inside the window and the facts match the headline; the trial is small and still human-guided.
importance_line: Shop staff, who spend 40 to 50 percent of their time refilling shelves according to Føtex, could eventually hand much of that repetitive work to robots, which the retailer says would free them to help customers, but for now the machines are operated by human controllers, work more slowly than staff and are not yet allowed to work alone among shoppers.
summary: Euronews reports that Danish start-up Hive Robots is training humanoid robots built by China's Unitree to pick up products and place them on shelves at a Føtex supermarket near Copenhagen, part of a wider trial with Salling Group, Denmark's largest retailer, in which human operators have guided every movement since June so the AI can learn to handle different products. The goal is for the robots to restock on their own, mainly at night, by early 2027, but they still work more slowly than people, need close supervision, and Danish law would have to change before they could work autonomously among shoppers.
notes: Read in full via Euronews (fulltext). machine_action true with a caveat: the robots do pick-and-place work but are guided by human operators for now. The trial has run since June 2026.
